Hi Irene / Monica,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can lock down the POC scope: 

- Goal: Improve checkout assistant accuracy for address parsing + localized upsell suggestions in EN, ES, and PT-BR.
- Success criteria (we propose): 92% address parsing accuracy on our anonymized sample, and <5% drop in conversion rate when suggestions are shown vs. baseline.
- Data: Attached a small sample (greencart-data-sample-1.csv) with POS tags and locale column. We can provide a larger dump after NDA.
- Expected volume: ~1k inference/hour during peak; average 200/hr. Latency target: p95 < 350ms.

Questions:
1) Which open-source model do you recommend for the multilingual mix? We prefer staying on open models for now.
2) Fallback plan if the selected model misses locale-specific tokens (e.g., Brazilian addresses).
3) Estimated timeline and owners for a 4-week POC.

Would like to kick off next Tue if that works.

Best,
Alice
Product Manager, GreenCart

Hi Alice — great notes, thanks. Below is a concrete POC plan + recommended model choices and owners. I attached a lightweight success-metrics template to make acceptance explicit.

POC objective (4 weeks):
- Validate open-model-based inference for multilingual address parsing + contextual upsell prompt in EN/ES/PT-BR while meeting latency and conversion constraints.

Recommended model roster (initial):
- Primary model: Llama-2-13B (open checkpoint) quantized to int8 — good balance for structured extraction and contextual prompts in EN/ES.
- Locale-heavy fallback: Mistral 7B (fine-tune candidate) or a locale-specific small adapter for PT-BR; use as a fast fallback for Portuguese variants.
- Safety/quality guardrail: run a light reranker (cross-encoder style) using a distilled bert-base to filter low-confidence outputs.

Why this roster:
- Llama-2-13B covers generalization across languages and is robust for parsing tasks when paired with a tight prompt + extraction template.
- Mistral 7B as fallback keeps latency low and provides a different tokenization behavior for Portuguese.

Success criteria (proposed — fillable in attached template):
- Address parsing: precision/recall F1 >= 0.92 on held-out sample.
- Upsell suggestion quality: human-rated relevance >= 4/5 on a 200-sample audit.
- Latency: p95 < 350ms end-to-end for requests routed to primary; fallback calls should add <100ms overhead.
- Reliability: 99% request completion during test windows.

Owner & roles:
- Sales/Coordination: Irene Choi (AE) — POC cadence, acceptance criteria, procurement interface.
- Solution engineering: Ben Carter — inference config, local test harness, latency tuning.
- Customer success / onboarding: Monica Patel — data intake, evaluation labeling.
- Infra/ops contact: Connor O'Brien — scaling, routing, fallback policy config.

Key asks from GreenCart:
1) Confirm languages and volume assumptions (you indicated EN/ES/PT-BR and 1k peak/hr).
2) Share a redacted 5k-sample CSV for evaluation (we'll keep it in a gated Drive).
3) NDA/PO form for dedicated test capacity if required by procurement.

Suggested timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope + NDA.
- Week 1: data ingestion, baseline runs, initial tuning.
- Week 2: focused evaluation and reranker integration.
- Week 3: A/B run vs baseline conversion test.
- Week 4: readout + acceptance.

Next step: If that looks good I'll schedule a 30m kickoff (Ben + Monica + Connor + your data lead). Are you available Tue 10am PT (05/25)?

Thanks — attaching: poc-success-metrics-template.xlsx

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical notes from our side before the kickoff: 

- Model selection: L2-13B quantized to int8 should meet the accuracy/latency tradeoff with token and KV-cache tuning. We'll prepare two quantization profiles (speed vs. quality) for the run.
- Fallback implementation: configure smart routing by locale header — if confidence score < 0.6, route to Mistral 7B with a shorter prompt + locale-specific post-processing. This avoids full re-run on the big model.
- Latency budgeting: with batching disabled for low-latency paths, expect p95 ~280–330ms on our dedicated pool (GPU: A10G equivalent). We'll instrument p50/p95 and token-level breakdown in the console.
- Data needs: Please include a small sample of Portuguese addresses with variations (CEP formats, diacritics). The CSV you sent is a great start; a 5k sample with locale flag will help produce reliable metrics.
- Evaluation harness: Monica / GreenCart data team will label 200 items for upsell relevance. We'll provide an annotation sheet and share results in Drive.

I'll bring a runbook and test harness to the kickoff so we can run a quick baseline in the first hour.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
